about: What species each tree near a viewpoint's camera is (task 061), and each of the shooter's area's a photo shows (task 088), as a session saw it in the viewpoint's photo and the reference photos (refs/photos.json), as refs/buildings.json holds the facades seen; tools/trees.mjs's kindOf takes it before anything else. species: what each name is, its kind (tools/trees.mjs's KINDS) and whether it keeps its leaves (leaves: deciduous or evergreen); broadleaf is a broadleaf the photo can't name, conifer a conifer and evergreen an evergreen broadleaf. trees: each tree seen, at: its crown's middle as the world had it when it was seen (braga-map 1.26.0's cx, cz, or 1.36.0's for task 088's), which names the tree of the map whose crown's middle is nearest, within half its crown's width or 3 m; species null where it's hidden in the photo (behind a trunk, a building or other trees) or the photo's camera is too far out to tell which it is; seen: the photo it was looked at in (viewpoint:<id>, or a reference photo's id: task 088's trees-<photo>-<heading> are Mapillary's panoramas in leaf, tools/species.mjs summer); sure: false where the photo shows the tree small, dark, half hidden or bare, or the tree of the map is a piece of a bigger crown. Every tree within 60 m of a viewpoint's camera and in its view (tools/species.mjs) is here, but for the skylines'; and every one of the shooter's area's within 60 m of a photo's camera, in its view and in sight past the buildings (tools/species.mjs shooter). rows: a species lining a stretch of street, as photos along it show it: every tree whose trunk stands within `within` metres of `line` is of it, but those seen. areas: a species filling a place: every tree whose trunk stands in `ring`, but those seen and those of a row.

areas.name: Parque da Ponte
areas.notes: Its canopy from the chapel's Largo to the roundabout and round the bandstand: limes, their heart-shaped leaves against the sky and their crowns in flower in June (landmark-parque-da-ponte-2); a few planes among them (seen). COS2025 has the park's wood as a eucalyptus one.
